sections.intro: An open letter to the people responsible for campaign performance.

content_blocks.text: If you’ve spent any meaningful time running performance marketing, you probably don’t need another person explaining the importance of testing.

You know your customers don’t all buy for the same reasons. You know your best campaign probably represents only a fraction of the purchasing motivations you could explore. And you almost certainly have people on your team who have already suggested some of them.
Knowing what might work and having the capacity to test it properly are two very different things.

Another creative? Fine. Another headline? Manageable. An entirely different buying motivation, carried consistently from the advertisement through the landing page, conversion experience and follow-up? That’s a project.

Someone needs to develop the argument. Someone needs to write it. Someone needs to design the creative. Someone needs to build the landing page. Someone needs to coordinate the follow-up. Someone needs to make sure everything is measurable. And all those people already have jobs to do.

So the idea joins the queue. Or gets simplified into another advert pointing at the existing landing page. Or disappears altogether. Not because it wasn’t worth testing. Because the organisation couldn’t afford to interrupt everything else to find out.
And that costs more than production time.

It means you keep spending money against the purchasing motivations you’ve already discovered, while potentially better ones remain unexplored. It means campaigns can become increasingly dependent on familiar propositions, even as their performance begins to deteriorate. It means your team is asked to extract more performance from the same arguments, rather than being given the capacity to investigate new ones.

And eventually, it means difficult conversations. Why isn’t the pipeline stronger? Why are leads becoming harder to convert? Why does the sales team keep questioning quality? Why are acquisition costs rising? Why haven’t we found another approach?

Sometimes the problem isn’t that you’ve failed to optimise the campaigns you’re running. It’s that you haven’t been able to run enough meaningfully different campaigns to understand what else could work.
Another software platform isn’t necessarily the answer.

Your team probably has the tools it needs. What it doesn’t necessarily have is spare capacity to operate another production process. A new AI platform might produce landing pages faster. Another might generate creative variations. Another might automate follow-up. Each can be useful.

But somebody still needs to bring the thinking together, preserve the message across the journey, assess the quality and coordinate the experiment. And now you’ve introduced another system to learn, another workflow to establish and another thing for somebody to own.
I think most marketing leaders want the work done. Properly. Without creating another operational problem.
That’s why we built Sorted.

I spent years working in marketing, including as Head of Marketing at Bisk Education. I’ve experienced the distance between knowing what a campaign needs and having the resources available to make it happen.

Sorted was built around a simple idea: what if manufacturing another complete campaign angle wasn’t a major undertaking? Not another random set of AI-generated advertisements. A genuine purchasing hypothesis—developed into convincing advertising, relevant creative, a dedicated landing experience, matching follow-up messaging and the measurement requirements needed to test it.

And rather than asking your team to coordinate all of that, we take responsibility for manufacturing the agreed assets. You keep your campaigns, your technology, your customers and your judgement. We supply the work.
Here’s where we start.

Give us two active products or campaigns you believe have room to improve. For one, we’ll explore an additional motivation within the existing proposition. For the other, we’ll develop an entirely different reason somebody might buy.

We’ll show you the proposed campaign directions before full production. Once they’re approved, we’ll build the agreed advertising assets, landing pages and follow-up narratives, with a measurement and activation handover.

Your team runs the experiments. You see what resonates, what attracts the right people and what deserves further investment. We don’t know in advance which angle will win. That’s why we’re testing. But we can make it more practical to find out.
Your next meaningful improvement might not be a better version of the campaign you’re already running. It might be a conversation with customers you’ve never properly had.
